name: FIXED_SENTENCE
status: W12 validation; frozen final policy; reserved confirmation separately reported
equation: Sort exact source sentences by descending query cosine; tentatively add each sentence if serialized evidence tokens remain ≤B. There is no fixed top-k restriction (C2 is the separate top-eight control).
purpose: Strong simple policy that distributes a limited budget across query-relevant sentences.
steps: Use the frozen SFR candidate pool and its exact sentences.
Rank by descending query-sentence similarity; ties use document order, start offset and stable ID.
Trial-serialize every candidate; skip non-fitting sentences and continue.
Serialize selected units into source-ordered per-passage blocks, then supply their exact token IDs to Qwen.
complexity: Cosine scoring O(Nd), sorting O(N log N), plus repeated tokenizer/serialization costs; not a knapsack solver.
strength: Simple, exact source text, budget-safe and chosen by the validation-time freeze.
limit: Semantic similarity need not identify downstream usefulness; irrelevant/redundant evidence can remain.
hyper: Configured candidate width10; evidence budgets256/1024; same frozen reader/decoder. No learned allocation threshold.
claim: Do not claim sentence evidence always beats passage evidence, or that the frozen choice is universally optimal.

name: QBGF_FULL / QBGF_NO_QUERY
status: W12 validation and ablation; not the universally frozen final policy
equation: R_i=exp(5p_i)/Σ_l exp(5p_l); w_ij=exp(5s_ij)/Σ_t exp(5s_it); m_i(a)=Σ_selected w_ij; U_i(a)=R_i m_i(a). DROP has utility0; FULL has mass1. Maximize Σ_i U_i(a_i), one action per passage, subject to Σ_i c_i(a_i)≤B.
purpose: Choose how faithfully to expose each retrieved source jointly under a shared token budget.
steps: Lab.prepare constructs the SFR-ranked pool, passage scores and sentence scores.
options creates DROP, SENT_1/2/4/8 and FULL, deduplicating identical short-source sentence states.
block computes exact token-ID costs including the trailing double newline.
solve runs multiple-choice dynamic programming over attainable integer costs.
choose serializes selected source representations and asserts additive cost consistency.
Reader.generate injects those evidence IDs into the frozen Qwen prompt.
complexity: DP transition count is bounded by O(P×B×A), with sparse attainable-cost states; Python tuple-path copying adds overhead. Exact only for this static surrogate and serializer.
strength: Explicit global budget optimization and interpretable per-source fidelity choices.
limit: The optimized relevance-mass surrogate is not answer utility; fusion did not establish robust universal superiority.
hyper: SENT counts1,2,4,8; softmax multiplication factors5/5; budgets256/1024; exact tie tolerances/order remain in solve.
claim: Do not say QBGF was the frozen final method, or that NO_QUERY removes query information from SFR retrieval.

name: BEA_QBGF_V1
status: POST-W12 exploratory; pilot50/dataset and expansion150/dataset are distinct
equation: IG(s|E)=Rel(s,q)+0.5Σ_a max(0,cos(a,s)−coverage_a(E))−0.5 max_{e∈E}cos(s,e); coverage_a(E)=max(0,max_{e∈E}cos(a,e)). M=IG/Δserialized_tokens for positive cost.
purpose: Reduce redundant exposure and add query-aspect coverage using recomputed context-dependent gains.
steps: Derive up to six query-only rule-based aspects and normalized query/sentence/aspect similarities.
Recompute every unselected sentence’s relevance, positive coverage gain and maximum redundancy against current E.
Trial-serialize candidate additions to get exact incremental token cost.
Only after at least two positive source-sentence selections can FULL compete; evaluate its missing sentences sequentially in source order.
Choose the globally best admissible marginal gain/cost with the actual deterministic tie order.
Stop when no admissible action remains; record LOW_MARGINAL_VALUE, budget and other reasons.
complexity: Dense pairwise cosine signals require O(N²) memory; each iteration rescans candidates and repeatedly serializes contexts. No exact global-optimum claim.
strength: Context-dependent redundancy/coverage and auditable stop/upgrade traces.
limit: Aspects can collapse to one; premature stopping, fragmentation and source escalation are task-dependent failure risks.
hyper: Effective frozen eta=.5, lambda=.5, tau_stop=.01, tau_expand=.01, tau_context=.05, min_parent_sentences2. The config file’s initial defaults are not the effective freeze.
claim: Do not call V1 a successful universal final system, or describe it as V2’s fixed1→2→4→8 state algorithm.

name: BEA_V2
status: Official calibration failed; tau8e-5 reader study is a separate post-hoc exploratory branch
equation: P_help=σ(βᵀ StandardScaler(x)+b); U(s|E)=P_help(s)×max(0,IG(s|E)); transition value=Σ_hypothetical additions U; M=transition value/Δserialized_tokens.
purpose: Weight semantic information gain by group-held-out predictions of historical LOO helpfulness.
steps: data.audit/feature_rows map historical exact-sentence deletion labels to inference-time source/query features.
models.train uses deterministic five-fold GroupKFold, scaler fit only in training folds, separate logistic help/harm models.
models.predict routes each known query/group to its held-out model and verifies training exclusion.
sequence re-ranks after every hypothetical addition; allocate considers next cumulative1/2/4/8 states and eligible FULL transitions.
P_harm is persisted diagnostically but is not subtracted from P_help.
The original nine-query mechanical calibration and single resolution sweep failed unchanged eligibility; the reader branch at8e-5 is explicitly post-hoc.
complexity: Training consists of fixed logistic fits over grouped historical unit rows. Allocation retains O(N²) pairwise signals plus repeated hypothetical re-ranking and serialization; not exact static MCKP.
strength: Separates predictive usefulness from semantic relevance with group isolation and inspectable transition values.
limit: Predictors are imbalanced historical context-specific surrogates; calibration failed. predict rejects unseen queries without a separately frozen all-development model.
hyper: 5folds; C1, L2, lbfgs, max_iter1000, no class weighting; eta=lambda=.5; states1,2,4,8; min parent2. No officially qualified tau. Post-hoc tau=.00008 only.
claim: Do not call V2 calibrated, freshly confirmed, causal-help probability, universally superior or deployable on arbitrary unseen queries.

name: MINILM_CE_SENTENCE
equation: r_j=CrossEncoder(q,s_j) raw logit; static descending ranking followed by exact serialize-and-skip packing under B. No softmax, P_help, aspect gain or gold-dependent selection.
purpose: Test a stronger query–sentence relevance scorer against embedding/cosine selection on the same source cohort.
steps: Load the original frozen pool/sentences, without rerunning or changing upstream selection.
Score each query/sentence pair using the pinned MiniLM cross-encoder on FP32 CPU.
Sort by raw score, passage retrieval rank, source position and stable ID.
Trial-serialize sentences using the same Qwen token-ID block serializer; skip non-fitting candidates.
Restore source presentation order and use the unchanged Qwen answer reader.
complexity: One transformer pair per sentence, length capped512; sorting O(N log N); repeated exact packing costs remain. No serving-throughput claim.
strength: Simple strong relevance control; no trained utility/aspect/stopping machinery.
limit: Static relevance still is not context-specific utility. It wins SciFact matched point estimates, but no comparison survives its recorded24-family Holm correction.
hyper: ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2 pinned revision; FP32 CPU; pair max512; raw identity logits; configured batch_size in protocol; evidence256/1024.
claim: Do not call MiniLM a universally better allocator or fresh confirmation. Its tie rule differs from FIXED_SENTENCE even though the serializer/fit-skip packing are shared.
